note: Mostly timbered upland in Clark County on gravel road 257. Camping is on or beside the area's two small roadside parking lots, about 250 m apart, each with MDC's primitive camping point in the trees beside it; farmsteads sit across the road from both. No pads and no amenities. --Claude
summary: Confirmed with a caveat: the brochure allows camping 'on or adjacent to all area parking lots and in designated camping areas', and GIS has a 'Primitive Camping Area' point in the woods ~40 m from each of the two small roadside lots; the map draws no camping symbol. Free/FCFS/no hookups/14 nights now manual. Phone matches; not waterfront kept; pin is under canopy - move 41 m onto the lot.
flags: CRITERIA (lot-side camping; owner's call between the Lick Creek keep and the lot-rule drop): area page 'Things to Do: Camping: Open Camping - Walk-in/Float-in/Backpack | Designated Camping Sites'; brochure 'Camping is allowed on or adjacent to all area parking lots and in designated camping areas. No unattended open campfires allowed. No amenities are provided.' The map (Last Updated 3/15/2022) legend has Parking Lot, Pond, Powerline, MDC Service Road - no camping symbol; it draws two parking lots on road 257. GIS 27 has two 'Primitive Camping Area' points: 1059 (= stored pin, 41 m NE of lot 1311) and 1056 (40.32327,-91.75055, ~45 m from the west pull-off). So MDC does mark designated points beside the lots (which keeps it under the 2026-11-09 rule), but the brochure's wording is the parking-lot wording that dropped other areas, and there is no pad at either point. I read it as a keep with the caveat in the note.

PIN (41 m move out of the woods): stored 40.32409,-91.74792 = GIS 1059, under closed canopy on leaf-on imagery, nothing visible. Lot 1311 (40.32388,-91.74832) is the small gravel lot on the north side of road 257 with a grass opening running north from it; suggested pin 40.32388,-91.74832. A 23-ft rig reaches either lot from Highway 81 on 2 miles of gravel road 257; no ford or limit on the map or brochure.
CLUSTERS: two lot-side spots ~250 m apart on the same road; one entry, no split. Neither is a main camp. Houses and farm buildings stand 50-80 m across the road from both.
WATERFRONT: not waterfront kept (upland timber; the pond by the west lot is a private pond across the road).
HORSES: none named in the brochure.
PHONE: page '(573) 248-2530' matches stored (and the brochure).
The page says 315 acres ('About 87 acres were recently added to the northeast part'); the 3/15/2022 map still says 227 acres and may not show features on the added tract.
NOTE: rewritten; dropped the 14-day limit (booking.max_stay_nights), the acreage, '2 camping spots' boilerplate, 'Site length not published', the inclusion boilerplate and the directions.
